bull_bear.body: - Focus on **profitable growth + return-on-capital** discipline ("intelligent scale, not scale for scale"); exiting sub-threshold business (Mumbai airport taxi, low-margin LMD). ROCE improving, to be shared at H1. No dividend/buyback discussion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **B2B Express breakeven still unproven** — confident but no committed quarter; GM-to-EBITDA flow-through was muted this quarter on ad-hoc manpower cost.
- **Contract-Logistics margin** — is 6.9% the "new normal" or does start-up cost fully reverse? Management says temporary; watch H2 recovery.
- **M&M concentration ~60%** (up from <50% as M&M outperforms) — cyclicality risk if M&M auto/tractor slows; management has *no target* to reduce it.
- **Freight Forwarding** — −39%, still rebuilding post-attrition + geopolitical drag.
- **Manpower availability + fuel volatility** — Q1 labour shortage (LPG/reverse-migration); fuel pass-through lag on the long B2B tail.
- **Mobility structurally lower-margin** — ETS-heavy mix caps margin vs peers (see §13).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, execution-focused, disciplined — Sikka repeatedly anchored on "profitable/intelligent scale" and refused to chase vanity volume (stopped disclosing Express tonnage on purpose; won't reverse-engineerable yield splits). Candid on the temporary cost bunching and honest that cross-sell/synergies are "still a lot of work." Frames M&M concentration as an outcome, not a target ("I'd like to win 100% of M&M and 100% of non-M&M"). Sober, credible turnaround narrative with concrete glide paths (white space, Express breakeven). Structurally bullish on Indian 3PL formalization.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The margin dip is a *growth* signal, not deterioration** — Contract-Logistics GM diluted *because* they opened a new site "almost every week" (start-up cost precedes revenue by 3–4 months); the operating leverage sits in H2.
- **Express turnaround is yield-led, not volume-led** — management deliberately stopped disclosing volumes because "we can take unlimited volume and never break EBITDA if we ignore rupee/kg"; the GM-positive → EBITDA-breakeven glide is the real KPI.
- **Adjusted (Ind-AS-116) EBITDA is the honest number** — ₹57cr (2.8%) vs ₹115cr reported; management now leads with the post-lease figure, a governance positive.
- **M&M is a tailwind re-concentrating the book** — the ~50%→~60% drift is *because* M&M auto/tractor is outgrowing industry, not because non-M&M is lagging (non-M&M also winning marquee manufacturing/e-commerce).
- **Mobility's margin gap is structural** — heavily weighted to low-margin employee-transport vs the more lucrative chauffeur/on-call model a listed peer runs (see §13).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Pan-India network scale: 20.4+ mn sq. ft warehousing space, 220+ processing centres, 19,000+ pin code reach, 100+ operating locations
- Backing and legacy of the Mahindra Group (100+ countries, 3,20,000+ employees, 20 industries), providing brand trust and captive fellow-subsidiary business
- Asset-right operating model reducing capital intensity while retaining network flexibility
- Growing EV-led fleet (1,400+ EVs) supporting sustainable last-mile and mobility differentiation
- Technology platform (LogiOne) providing integrated end-to-end visibility across warehouses, transporters and customers as a stated differentiator
- Diversified multi-segment portfolio (3PL, Express, Last-Mile, Freight-Forwarding, Mobility) across resilient end-industries (auto, pharma, FMCG, telecom, e-commerce)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Governance/ethics conduct risk (whistle-blower complaints) — Company received 21 whistle-blower complaints during FY26; 13 were investigated with action taken, while investigations remained underway for the remaining 8 at year end, indicating an ongoing pipeline of conduct-related matters.
- Workplace conduct / legal risk (sexual harassment complaints) — 13 sexual harassment (POSH) complaints were received during FY26, of which 9 were disposed; 4 cases remained pending as of 31 March 2026 (none pending beyond 90 days), representing an ongoing workplace-conduct and legal-compliance exposure.
- Information and cyber security risk — The company's Risk Management Policy explicitly identifies information and cyber-security risks as a formal risk category, reflecting exposure inherent to its technology-enabled, digitally integrated logistics operations; no incidents were reported in FY26 but the exposure is structural given reliance on digital platforms for tracking and operations.
- Acquisition and integration risk — The Risk Management Policy was amended during FY26 to align with risks related to acquisitions and the increasing size and complexity of the Company's operations, reflecting integration risk from its growing base of subsidiaries and joint ventures.
- Broad multi-category enterprise risk exposure — Management's formal Risk Management Policy and framework cover Financial, Operational, Sectoral, Sustainability (ESG), Information and Cyber Security risks as the risk universe the Risk Management Committee monitors, indicating the breadth of structural risk categories considered material to the business.

outlook.body:
- 'Grow Responsibly' — embedding sustainability (renewable energy adoption, electrification, data analytics, circular economy principles) into operational decisions across the network
- Decarbonising delivery through multi-modal networks (increasing rail for long-haul), load consolidation, low-emission fuels (CNG, biodiesel), BS IV-to-BS VI fleet transition, and EV-led electrification of last-mile and mobility fleets
- PAHAL — a Sustainable Supply Chain Management (SSCM) programme extending sustainability commitments beyond MLL's own operations into its supplier and Business Associate (BA) network, using a dedicated SaaS platform for data collection and assessment
- Customer-centric engagement model: quarterly Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) tracking across business lines, CRM/analytics-led sales, pricing and account management, and LOGIPace digital complaint-management platform
- Continued technology investment as a differentiator — LogiOpt (analytics/IT platform recognised at IIM Mumbai), Logi RYD (AI-enabled B2B employee transportation platform), and the rebranded Alyte B2C mobility app (formerly Meru)
- Deepening focus on complex, integrated end-market solutions (auto, farm & manufacturing, e-commerce/q-commerce, consumer, telecom, pharma) as supply chains grow more complex and customers seek fewer, more capable logistics partners
- Continued investment in leadership pipeline and workforce capability (LEAP, FLEX, LAMP programmes) to support scale and diversification
- Company follows a disciplined capital allocation philosophy anchored on strengthening the balance sheet, deleveraging and return-driven reinvestment: following the successful Rights Issue (completed August 2025), the Company eliminated debt at the standalone level and significantly reduced consolidated borrowings, substantially de-risking the balance sheet and cost of capital. Capital deployment is guided by a Capital Allocation Framework with strict return thresholds, prioritising investments with clear paths to margin expansion, alongside a selective 'asset-right' approach to owned-asset investment. The Board recommended a dividend for the year (25% of face value), reflecting an intent to balance growth investment with shareholder returns.

outlook.body: During FY26, MLL commissioned Grade A warehousing facilities in Guwahati and Agartala to strengthen eastern India connectivity, and commissioned a ~4 lakh sq. ft. warehouse in Phaltan for Cummins India, serving as its India Logistics Centre. The company also launched a ~4 lakh sq. ft. facility for the 2X2 Logistics business to strengthen operational capacity and support future growth, and inducted 50 new vehicles. On the Mobility side, MLL launched Alyte Privé, a premium and tech-enabled people mobility service. The company describes an 'Asset-Right Transition' strategy — selectively investing in owned assets where control drives superior yields, while retaining flexibility across its broader (largely asset-light/business-associate-based) network — guided by a Capital Allocation Framework with strict return thresholds prioritising investments with clear paths to margin expansion.

outlook.body:
- India's e-commerce market expected to grow at ~15% CAGR to reach ~₹30 lakh crores by 2030; q-commerce growing ~70-80% annually, driving demand for hyperlocal fulfilment, dense last-mile networks and dark stores (6,000+)
- Auto, Farm and Manufacturing sectors recorded ~13% YoY growth; domestic tractor sales up ~19% YoY to ~10 lakh units and four-wheeler EV sales up ~84% to ~2 lakh units, supported by the PLI scheme and 'Make-in-India' initiatives
- India's consumer goods sector expected to grow 6-8% in 2025-26, aided by PLI allocations for food processing (~₹1,200 crores) and white goods (~₹1,000 crores) and GST reductions on consumer products
- Telecom sector (India's 2nd-largest globally, ~120 crore subscribers) expanding at ~7% CAGR on continued 5G rollout and fibre expansion, generating logistics demand across network equipment and infrastructure deployment
- Pharma sector (India supplies ~20% of global generics demand) projected to reach ~₹11 lakh crores by 2030 (~10% CAGR), with PLI schemes for APIs/bulk drugs strengthening domestic supply chains and driving demand for temperature-controlled, compliance-led logistics
- India's GDP growth for 2025-26 estimated at 7.4%, supported by strong consumption and investment; public capital expenditure of ~₹11 lakh crores in 2025-26 and ~₹12.2 lakh crores proposed for 2026-27 reaffirm an infrastructure-led growth model (PM GatiShakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Multimodal Logistics Parks, inland waterways) that is translating into logistics sector expansion
- Logistics sector remains highly fragmented with road transport dominant (60%+ of freight), while rail, air and waterways gain share through policy support; demand for Grade A/B warehousing, multimodal integration, AI-driven optimisation and digital freight solutions is rising, alongside an influx of institutional capital into Grade A warehousing assets
- Global growth remains moderated (2.7% in 2026, 2.9% in 2027, below pre-pandemic levels), with elevated sovereign debt, trade fragmentation and geopolitical conflict introducing volatility into energy prices, freight costs and global supply chains; trade dynamics are shifting toward near-shoring and resilience-led network design, with businesses increasingly deploying AI-driven optimisation and multinode supply chains

one-line thesis: The transformation has "evolved into a growth journey": **PAT swung to +₹25.4cr from a −₹10.8cr loss** a year ago on +23% revenue, with the loss-making **B2B Express (Rivigo) turning gross-margin positive** (+₹9.2cr vs −₹3.6cr) and on track for **EBITDA breakeven this year**. Contract Logistics grew 26% (EBITDA +31%) but gross margin diluted ~46bps on *temporary* start-up/manpower/fuel-lag costs (~half is new-site ramp that normalizes). Management reaffirms a **150–200bps medium-term gross-margin expansion** and the **95%-white-space-reduction glide path by Sep-2026**, while leaning harder into disciplined, profitable ("intelligent scale") growth across a diversifying (M&M ~60%) book.
financial scorecard (q1 fy27):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | **₹2,003cr** | **+23%** | SCM 94% / Mobility 6% |
| Gross margin | **9.7%** (GP ₹194.5cr) | +28bps (from 9.4%) | |
| Reported EBITDA | **₹115cr** | from ₹76cr | |
| Adjusted EBITDA (Ind-AS 116) | **₹57cr · 2.8%** | **+76%** (from ₹32cr), +85bps | post full lease cost |
| PAT | **₹25.4cr** | vs **−₹10.8cr** (+₹36cr) | incl. ₹4cr **one-off** tax-refund interest → **operating PAT ~₹21.4cr** |
> One-offs/distortions: (a) **₹4cr non-recurring** interest on income-tax refund in other income (operating PAT ~₹21.4cr); (b) Contract-Logistics gross margin diluted ~46bps on a **temporary bunching** of new-site start-up costs (~half the dilution), Q1 **manpower shortage** (LPG shortage + reverse migration → ad-hoc labour), min-wage revisions, and **fuel-price pass-through lag**; (c) Freight Forwarding hit by customer attrition (transition) + geopolitical crisis.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **B2B Express (Rivigo): EBITDA breakeven within FY27** — "very confident of achieving"; PAT progression to follow in a calibrated manner (won't commit a specific quarter).
- **White space: reduce by 95% by September 2026** (vs the 1.6M sq ft base of Q1 last year) — "firmly on track."
- **Overall gross margin: +150–200 bps** expansion over the medium term.
- **Continue PAT-positivity + operating improvement** — revenue & PAT growth as the stated trajectory.
- **Contract Logistics margin recovery** — start-up/ramp costs (temporary) to normalize through the year; efficiencies to be recovered.
- **Mobility: work toward 9–10% gross margin**; EBITDA-% to improve with scale/operating leverage (+ B2B investments).
- **ROCE improving** — to be disclosed at H1 (Q2); no forward ROCE guidance.
- Airport-taxi (Alyte): scale **only where profitable** — doubling down on Delhi + Noida (preferred partner), **exiting Mumbai** (below internal threshold).
order book & pipeline: - Not a classic order-book business. Growth signals: Contract-Logistics new-site wins **"exceeded the aggressive Q1 stretch plan"** (opening a new site "almost every week"); a **~2-lakh-sq-ft marquee site at Luhari (Gurgaon)** ramping; "a couple of very large marquee manufacturing clients" won last quarter. Warehousing footprint ~**21M sq ft**, high utilisation.
segment / subsidiary detail (q1 fy27):
- **Contract Logistics — ₹1,623cr (+26%).** Drivers: M&M auto+farm momentum + e-commerce + **manufacturing/telecom** vertical. GM diluted ~46bps (start-up ~half, manpower, min-wage, fuel-lag) but **EBITDA +31%**, margin **6.6%→6.9%** (overhead efficiency/operating leverage offset).
- **B2B Express (MESPL/Rivigo) — ₹152cr (+58%).** Volume + yield both up; **GM 6% vs −3.8%**; EBITDA loss cut to **−₹1.6cr (from −₹11.8cr)**; GM +120bps QoQ (from 4.8%). Turnaround focus = yield discipline, *not* volume-chasing (stopped disclosing volumes deliberately).
- **Last-Mile Delivery — revenue −16% (deliberate).** Exited low-margin business; **GM 5%→9%**; stays EBITDA-positive.
- **Freight Forwarding — ₹45cr (−39%).** Customer attrition (transition) + geopolitical crisis; **GM ~10% held** (historical); EBITDA-positive; leadership strengthened, pipeline rebuilding.
- **Mobility — ₹111cr (+38%).** B2B (employee transport) client-base expansion; GM +2%; historically 9–10% GM but **ETS-heavy** (lower margin than the chauffeur/on-call mix). Alyte B2C: exit Mumbai airport, scale Delhi + Noida.
growth verticals / optionality: - **B2B Express turnaround** (Rivigo → EBITDA breakeven, then PAT) · **e-commerce / quick-commerce** 3PL (strong wins) · **manufacturing & telecom** vertical (MSME + large) · **cross-sell** of all MLL verticals into 3PL customers (Sikka's stated objective; "a lot of work still to be done") · **airport-taxi** (Alyte, profitable airports only) · **LogiOne** tech/digital ecosystem · **non-M&M** client acquisition (a core focus alongside winning "100% of M&M").
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Mahindra Group parentage** — governance + reliability that "customers value a lot"; anchor M&M (world's largest tractor company by volume) provides a structural tailwind and a manufacturing-logistics core competence transferable to other manufacturers.
- **Solutioning + execution + tech (LogiOne)** — wins are "hard-fought national RFQs," not pure-price; reputation/governance cited as differentiators.
- **3PL scale in an unorganized market** — positioned to gain as the sector formalizes (see §13).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Consolidated GM 9.7% (+28bps). Contract-Logistics GM dilution (~46bps) is **temporary bunching**: ~half = new-site start-up (3–4 months to normalize on large sites; ~2 weeks on small; ~10 days for tiny LMD sites), rest = Q1 manpower spike + fuel-lag.
- Fuel is a **pass-through**: M&M repriced within 48 hrs on the ₹8.10 hike; B2B Express (long tail of hundreds of customers) **~80% passed on** — the residual is a near-term GM headwind that reverses as pass-through completes.
- Overhead/opex efficiency partly offsetting GM dilution at the EBITDA line; **150–200bps GM expansion** targeted medium-term.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Asset-light bias; warehousing ~21M sq ft (Ind-AS-116 capitalisation drove the YoY depreciation step-up, in line sequentially). New large 3PL sites (Luhari) + airport-taxi (Delhi/Noida) the visible adds. No large capex figure flagged.
capital allocation: - Focus on **profitable growth + return-on-capital** discipline ("intelligent scale, not scale for scale"); exiting sub-threshold business (Mumbai airport taxi, low-margin LMD). ROCE improving, to be shared at H1. No dividend/buyback discussion.
risks & watch-items:
- **B2B Express breakeven still unproven** — confident but no committed quarter; GM-to-EBITDA flow-through was muted this quarter on ad-hoc manpower cost.
- **Contract-Logistics margin** — is 6.9% the "new normal" or does start-up cost fully reverse? Management says temporary; watch H2 recovery.
- **M&M concentration ~60%** (up from <50% as M&M outperforms) — cyclicality risk if M&M auto/tractor slows; management has *no target* to reduce it.
- **Freight Forwarding** — −39%, still rebuilding post-attrition + geopolitical drag.
- **Manpower availability + fuel volatility** — Q1 labour shortage (LPG/reverse-migration); fuel pass-through lag on the long B2B tail.
- **Mobility structurally lower-margin** — ETS-heavy mix caps margin vs peers (see §13).
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, disciplined — Sikka repeatedly anchored on "profitable/intelligent scale" and refused to chase vanity volume (stopped disclosing Express tonnage on purpose; won't reverse-engineerable yield splits). Candid on the temporary cost bunching and honest that cross-sell/synergies are "still a lot of work." Frames M&M concentration as an outcome, not a target ("I'd like to win 100% of M&M and 100% of non-M&M"). Sober, credible turnaround narrative with concrete glide paths (white space, Express breakeven). Structurally bullish on Indian 3PL formalization.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The margin dip is a *growth* signal, not deterioration** — Contract-Logistics GM diluted *because* they opened a new site "almost every week" (start-up cost precedes revenue by 3–4 months); the operating leverage sits in H2.
- **Express turnaround is yield-led, not volume-led** — management deliberately stopped disclosing volumes because "we can take unlimited volume and never break EBITDA if we ignore rupee/kg"; the GM-positive → EBITDA-breakeven glide is the real KPI.
- **Adjusted (Ind-AS-116) EBITDA is the honest number** — ₹57cr (2.8%) vs ₹115cr reported; management now leads with the post-lease figure, a governance positive.
- **M&M is a tailwind re-concentrating the book** — the ~50%→~60% drift is *because* M&M auto/tractor is outgrowing industry, not because non-M&M is lagging (non-M&M also winning marquee manufacturing/e-commerce).
- **Mobility's margin gap is structural** — heavily weighted to low-margin employee-transport vs the more lucrative chauffeur/on-call model a listed peer runs (see §13).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's e-commerce market expected to grow at ~15% CAGR to reach ~₹30 lakh crores by 2030; q-commerce growing ~70-80% annually, driving demand for hyperlocal fulfilment, dense last-mile networks and dark stores (6,000+)
- Auto, Farm and Manufacturing sectors recorded ~13% YoY growth; domestic tractor sales up ~19% YoY to ~10 lakh units and four-wheeler EV sales up ~84% to ~2 lakh units, supported by the PLI scheme and 'Make-in-India' initiatives
- India's consumer goods sector expected to grow 6-8% in 2025-26, aided by PLI allocations for food processing (~₹1,200 crores) and white goods (~₹1,000 crores) and GST reductions on consumer products
- Telecom sector (India's 2nd-largest globally, ~120 crore subscribers) expanding at ~7% CAGR on continued 5G rollout and fibre expansion, generating logistics demand across network equipment and infrastructure deployment
- Pharma sector (India supplies ~20% of global generics demand) projected to reach ~₹11 lakh crores by 2030 (~10% CAGR), with PLI schemes for APIs/bulk drugs strengthening domestic supply chains and driving demand for temperature-controlled, compliance-led logistics
- India's GDP growth for 2025-26 estimated at 7.4%, supported by strong consumption and investment; public capital expenditure of ~₹11 lakh crores in 2025-26 and ~₹12.2 lakh crores proposed for 2026-27 reaffirm an infrastructure-led growth model (PM GatiShakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Multimodal Logistics Parks, inland waterways) that is translating into logistics sector expansion
- Logistics sector remains highly fragmented with road transport dominant (60%+ of freight), while rail, air and waterways gain share through policy support; demand for Grade A/B warehousing, multimodal integration, AI-driven optimisation and digital freight solutions is rising, alongside an influx of institutional capital into Grade A warehousing assets
- Global growth remains moderated (2.7% in 2026, 2.9% in 2027, below pre-pandemic levels), with elevated sovereign debt, trade fragmentation and geopolitical conflict introducing volatility into energy prices, freight costs and global supply chains; trade dynamics are shifting toward near-shoring and resilience-led network design, with businesses increasingly deploying AI-driven optimisation and multinode supply chains

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Consolidated GM 9.7% (+28bps). Contract-Logistics GM dilution (~46bps) is **temporary bunching**: ~half = new-site start-up (3–4 months to normalize on large sites; ~2 weeks on small; ~10 days for tiny LMD sites), rest = Q1 manpower spike + fuel-lag.
- Fuel is a **pass-through**: M&M repriced within 48 hrs on the ₹8.10 hike; B2B Express (long tail of hundreds of customers) **~80% passed on** — the residual is a near-term GM headwind that reverses as pass-through completes.
- Overhead/opex efficiency partly offsetting GM dilution at the EBITDA line; **150–200bps GM expansion** targeted medium-term.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, MLL commissioned Grade A warehousing facilities in Guwahati and Agartala to strengthen eastern India connectivity, and commissioned a ~4 lakh sq. ft. warehouse in Phaltan for Cummins India, serving as its India Logistics Centre. The company also launched a ~4 lakh sq. ft. facility for the 2X2 Logistics business to strengthen operational capacity and support future growth, and inducted 50 new vehicles. On the Mobility side, MLL launched Alyte Privé, a premium and tech-enabled people mobility service. The company describes an 'Asset-Right Transition' strategy — selectively investing in owned assets where control drives superior yields, while retaining flexibility across its broader (largely asset-light/business-associate-based) network — guided by a Capital Allocation Framework with strict return thresholds prioritising investments with clear paths to margin expansion.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, disciplined — Sikka repeatedly anchored on "profitable/intelligent scale" and refused to chase vanity volume (stopped disclosing Express tonnage on purpose; won't reverse-engineerable yield splits). Candid on the temporary cost bunching and honest that cross-sell/synergies are "still a lot of work." Frames M&M concentration as an outcome, not a target ("I'd like to win 100% of M&M and 100% of non-M&M"). Sober, credible turnaround narrative with concrete glide paths (white space, Express breakeven). Structurally bullish on Indian 3PL formalization.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pan-India network scale: 20.4+ mn sq. ft warehousing space, 220+ processing centres, 19,000+ pin code reach, 100+ operating locations
- Backing and legacy of the Mahindra Group (100+ countries, 3,20,000+ employees, 20 industries), providing brand trust and captive fellow-subsidiary business
- Asset-right operating model reducing capital intensity while retaining network flexibility
- Growing EV-led fleet (1,400+ EVs) supporting sustainable last-mile and mobility differentiation
- Technology platform (LogiOne) providing integrated end-to-end visibility across warehouses, transporters and customers as a stated differentiator
- Diversified multi-segment portfolio (3PL, Express, Last-Mile, Freight-Forwarding, Mobility) across resilient end-industries (auto, pharma, FMCG, telecom, e-commerce)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:

- **Freight Forwarding** — −39%, still rebuilding post-attrition + geopolitical drag.
- **Manpower availability + fuel volatility** — Q1 labour shortage (LPG/reverse-migration); fuel pass-through lag on the long B2B tail.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The margin dip is a *growth* signal, not deterioration** — Contract-Logistics GM diluted *because* they opened a new site "almost every week" (start-up cost precedes revenue by 3–4 months); the operating leverage sits in H2.
- **Express turnaround is yield-led, not volume-led** — management deliberately stopped disclosing volumes because "we can take unlimited volume and never break EBITDA if we ignore rupee/kg"; the GM-positive → EBITDA-breakeven glide is the real KPI.
- **Adjusted (Ind-AS-116) EBITDA is the honest number** — ₹57cr (2.8%) vs ₹115cr reported; management now leads with the post-lease figure, a governance positive.
- **M&M is a tailwind re-concentrating the book** — the ~50%→~60% drift is *because* M&M auto/tractor is outgrowing industry, not because non-M&M is lagging (non-M&M also winning marquee manufacturing/e-commerce).
- **Mobility's margin gap is structural** — heavily weighted to low-margin employee-transport vs the more lucrative chauffeur/on-call model a listed peer runs (see §13).
